title.narrative: Second Phase of the Central Asia Road Links Program

description.narrative: The Central Asia Road Links (CARs) program has the overall development objective to increase transport connectivity between neighboring countries in Central Asia along priority cross-border road links and to support improvements in road operations and asset management practices. The program is the result of a collaborative effort initiated by respective governments in the Central Asia region which has been developed as a regional, multi-phase program considered as a regional project under IDA16 and IDA 17 with substantialtransformational impact. The project development objective (PDO) of the Second Phase of the Central Asia Road Links Program (CARs-2) is to increase transport connectivity between the Republic of Tajikistan and neighboring countries along priority cross-border road links in Sugd Oblast and to support improvements in road operations and asset management practices. The road sections to be financed under CARs-2 prioritize connectivity between Sugd Oblast in Tajikistan with Batken and Osh Oblasts in the Kyrgyz Republic and Ferghana Oblast in Uzbekistan.

The project development objective (PDO) of the Second Phase of the Central Asia Road Links Program (CARs-2) is to increase transport connectivity between the Republic of Tajikistan and neighboring countries along priority cross-border road links in Sugd Oblast and to support improvements in road operations and asset management practices. The road sections to be financed under CARs-2 prioritize connectivity between Sugd Oblast in Tajikistan with Batken and Osh Oblasts in the Kyrgyz Republic and Ferghana Oblast in Uzbekistan. The road sections to be financed under CARs-2 prioritize connectivity between the Sugd Oblast in Tajikistan and the Osh and Batken Oblasts in the Kyrgyz Republic as they build lateral spurs from the Khujand- Osh axis to the Kyrgyz border. The project consists of three components. Component one is expected to finance the provision of works and consultants? services for the rehabilitation of approximately 70 kilometers of road sections in Sugd Oblast. Component two is proposed to finance the provision of goods, and consultants? services for the improvement of road operations and asset management practices. Component three is expected to finance the provision of goods, consultants? services, and training, operating costs, including a financial audit to support project coordination, implementation, and management.

Volume of freight through Guliston/Kyzyl-Bel and Madaniyat/Kairagach, Patar border crossing points

comment.narrative: At the time of submitting the ISR, only the first half year of 2020 data have been aggregated. The second half traffic data will be aggregated after end of the year and added together for the full year number. Due to COVID-19 and related travel and trade restrctions, there has been a significant reduction in the traffic volume, which is considered temporary and expected to rebound once the pandemic is under control.

title.narrative: Market accessibility index of Sugd Oblast

comment.narrative:
Passengers component –This indicator measures the average market accessibility of Sugd Oblast, described as the sum of population of the selected major cities weighted by travel time to reach major markets. Major cities include Isfara, Kanibadam, and Khujand. Freight component – a freight component such as average travel times for a typical freight truck between Kanibadam to/from the Guliston/Kyzyl-Bel, from Dehmoy to/from Madniyat/Kairagach and from Kanibadam to/from Patar border control points.
The number will be updated during preparation of ICR, with support from the Bank team to repeat the analysis during preparation.

title.narrative: RAMS system is in operation for analysis and planning of road works

comment.narrative: <p>Road Asset Management Database System developed was put in operation. Hardware, machinery, and equipment required for the operation of RAMS were procured and installed, including servers, roughness profiler, and 40 traffic counts on the main roads in differentregions of the country. With the hardware supplied and installed under the project, MOT has started carrying out some RAMS activities. While additional support is needed to scale the data collection to the larger network and bring about institutional and organizational changes to ensure continued use of RAMS, some functionalities are in place for analysis and planning.</p>
